data.long_meaning: A person who has pledged or given a promise, often in the context of a religious or legal agreement. In Islamic tradition, this can refer to someone who has taken the Shahada, or declaration of faith, and has committed to living as a Muslim. The name Mukallaf carries the meaning “One who is bound by a contract or promise” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic.
